tasks.title: Move the read-failure helper to dicom_io and share it
tasks.test_approach: Move the existing helper unit tests (chunked read, missing file, forced PermissionError, ENOMEM -> MemoryError) to test_dicom_io.py against dicom_io.read_failure; retarget test_preprocess.py patches from pre.open / pre.READ_CHUNK / pre._read_failure to dicom_io.open / dicom_io.READ_CHUNK / dicom_io.read_failure. RED: the moved tests fail on the missing dicom_io.read_failure; GREEN after the move. Forced-error tests patch dicom_io.open path-selectively (raise only for the target file; every other path goes to builtins.open), binary mode, and run with workers=1 (a monkeypatch does not reach a spawned worker). POSIX chmod tests carry skipif(os.name != 'posix' or os.geteuid() == 0) and restore modes in a finally. Synthetic data only (tests/synthetic_dicom.py), generated at test time. preprocess no longer defines _read_failure or READ_CHUNK; read_image and read_info call dicom_io.read_failure through the module (not a from-import), after the except block, then raise the CaseRefused
Spec A11: every preprocess read-error test passes with its patches retargeted to dicom_io.open, dicom_io.READ_CHUNK and dicom_io.read_failure; no preprocess test is deleted, skipped or xfailed

tasks.title: Classify a failed convert input read (header, CT, dose, other series)
tasks.test_approach: End-to-end convert() runs on a synthetic organized tree (existing test_convert helpers). A1/A2: chmod 0 on a plan CT slice / a misc_files DICOM. Per-site failing fixture (a garbage file never gets past the header read, so it cannot reach the CT, dose or series reads): header read = a garbage-bytes file in the plan folder; CT = truncate_pixels (test_convert.py ~:721) -> REASON_CT_UNREADABLE; dose = resave_dose with DoseGridScaling=NaN (test_convert.py ~:1240) -> REASON_DOSE_UNREADABLE; series = a non-planning series written with the synthetic CT writer into misc_files with one slice's pixel data cut short (header intact) -> that series' study row skipped. A3: the same per-site fixture plus dicom_io.open raising PermissionError (and an EIO OSError) for that file only. A4: the per-site fixture alone keeps the existing reason. Root-safe twins for A1/A2: patch dicom_io.read_header_core to raise OSError(dicom_io.REASON_UNREADABLE) and dicom_io.open to raise PermissionError, both for that path only. A9 runs over A1 and over A3 at each site, with caplog.set_level(logging.DEBUG). A10's happy-path fixture holds an RTDOSE and a non-planning series in misc_files, so all four sites run. A5: ENOMEM OSError from dicom_io.open -> REASON_INTERNAL row and ConvertAborted. A9: caplog + report text contain neither the file path nor (outside the patient column) the patient folder name. A10: spy on dicom_io.read_failure over a happy-path convert. Each test RED first. Forced-error tests patch dicom_io.open path-selectively (raise only for the target file; every other path goes to builtins.open), binary mode, and run with workers=1 (a monkeypatch does not reach a spawned worker). POSIX chmod tests carry skipif(os.name != 'posix' or os.geteuid() == 0) and restore modes in a finally. Synthetic data only (tests/synthetic_dicom.py), generated at test time. Vault: [[simpleitk-read-errors-have-no-errno]].
criteria: convert._read_one: after read_header_core's OSError is caught, dicom_io.read_failure(path) runs after the except block; a clean re-read or a missing file still returns (path, None)
convert._read_ct calls dicom_io.read_failure on every slice path after quiet_call raised CaseRefused (after the except block), then re-raises the CaseRefused(REASON_CT_UNREADABLE)

convert._read_dose calls dicom_io.read_failure(path) after the extract quiet_call raised CaseRefused (after the except block), then re-raises CaseRefused(REASON_DOSE_UNREADABLE); the build step is not classified

series.py's series read calls dicom_io.read_failure on every slice path after the CaseRefused, after the except block, then returns None as today; the module docstring and the read_series docstring no longer claim that no exception escapes (an OSError from read_failure does)

tasks.title: Folder checks raise a permission error on every Python version
tasks.test_approach: Helper unit tests on real tmp_path entries (missing, dangling symlink, under a regular file, embedded NUL, chmod-0o444 parent). A6 and A8 patch Path.is_file and Path.is_dir to return False (Python 3.14's behaviour) so they are RED before the change on 3.13; root-safe twins patch Path.stat path-selectively to raise PermissionError for the target folder's entries only (never os.stat globally). A8 runs the CLI (test_cli.py's existing pattern) on a root with one patient folder. Forced-error tests patch dicom_io.open path-selectively (raise only for the target file; every other path goes to builtins.open), binary mode, and run with workers=1 (a monkeypatch does not reach a spawned worker). POSIX chmod tests carry skipif(os.name != 'posix' or os.geteuid() == 0) and restore modes in a finally. Synthetic data only (tests/synthetic_dicom.py), generated at test time. Vault: [[simpleitk-read-errors-have-no-errno]]. A8 runs in-process (a monkeypatch does not reach test_cli's subprocess runs): with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as e: cli.main(['convert', str(org), str(out)]); assert e.value.code == 1 and capsys err == 'rt_dataprep: file system error on the source or output root\n' (pattern of test_cli.py ~:294). The Path.is_file/Path.is_dir -> False patch is path-selective: False only for the 0o444 folder's entries (A6) or the root's entries (A8), delegating to the original for every other path (a global patch breaks Path.mkdir(exist_ok=True) and other unrelated calls). Every Path.stat patch has the signature (self, *, follow_symlinks=True) and delegates to the original for every other path. Root-safe twins: A7's EACCES case via Path.stat raising PermissionError; A6/A8 twins apply the same path-selective is_file/is_dir -> False patch plus Path.stat raising PermissionError for those entries, so they are RED before the change (Path.stat alone makes 3.13's unpatched is_dir raise, which passes pre-fix).
criteria: dicom_io has one helper (e.g. entry_is(path, kind)) that calls path.stat() and returns Python 3.13's is_file()/is_dir() result: False for ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EBADF, ELOOP and for ValueError; any other OSError is raised

convert's five folder checks use it through the module: the root's patient-folder listing, the patient's plan-folder listing, the misc_files check, read_folder_headers' file listing, and the misc_files listing for salvage; no Path.is_file/Path.is_dir call remains on convert's input side

Spec A6: with Path.is_file/Path.is_dir patched to return False, a plan folder with mode 0o444 gives the patient's REASON_IO_ERROR; the root-safe twin (Path.stat raising PermissionError for that folder's entries) gives the same
Spec A7: the helper returns False for a missing entry, a dangling symlink, an entry under a regular file and a name with an embedded NUL, and raises PermissionError for EACCES

Spec A8: with Path.is_file/Path.is_dir patched to return False, the organized root itself with mode 0o444, holding one patient folder, makes the CLI exit 1 with 'rt_dataprep: file system error on the source or output root' and the output root does not exist afterwards
uv run --group dev pytest -q --tb=short and ruff check . pass
